name: release

# Builds and publishes per-platform chisme binaries on a version tag.
#
# We use a per-OS matrix (one native runner per target) rather than cross-compiling
# from a single runner. Reason: the sqlite-vec loadable extension ships as
# per-platform npm packages that only install on a matching host, and build.ts
# embeds that native extension into the binary so semantic search works standalone.
# A single cross-compiling runner would only have its own platform's extension and
# would produce keyword-only binaries for every other target.

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    name: build ${{ matrix.asset }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { runner: ubuntu-latest, asset: chisme-linux-x64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm, asset: chisme-linux-arm64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: macos-15-intel, asset: chisme-darwin-x64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: macos-15, asset: chisme-darwin-arm64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: windows-latest, asset: chisme-windows-x64.exe, bin: chisme.exe }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.12

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      # Apple's system SQLite (which Bun uses on macOS) is built without loadable
      # extensions, so sqlite-vec can't load and semantic search degrades to
      # keyword-only. Compile a self-contained vanilla SQLite (FTS5 + extension
      # support, depends only on libSystem) for this runner's arch; build.ts embeds
      # it and the binary redirects bun:sqlite to it via Database.setCustomSQLite().
      - name: Build vanilla SQLite for macOS
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ver=3460100
          curl -fsSL "https://www.sqlite.org/2024/sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}.zip" -o sqlite.zip
          unzip -q sqlite.zip
          cc -O2 -dynamiclib \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS3 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS4 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_RTREE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_DESERIALIZE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS \
            -DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 \
            -install_name @rpath/libsqlite3.dylib \
            "sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}/sqlite3.c" \
            -o "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          file "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          otool -L "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          echo "CHISME_MACOS_SQLITE_DYLIB=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Build native binary
        run: bun run build:cli

      - name: Stage release asset
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          mv "${{ matrix.bin }}" "dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"

      - name: Smoke test (standalone hybrid search end to end)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"
          "$bin" version
          # Index only the newest few checkpoints so the test stays fast as the
          # repo's history grows (chisme sync fetches entire/checkpoints/v1 from
          # origin). Then assert the embedded semantic search actually ran: with a
          # small indexed set, vec KNN returns those checkpoints for any query, so
          # a working embedder yields a "both" or "semantic" match. A broken one
          # yields only "keyword" (or nothing) and fails the build, so a semantic
          # regression cannot ship silently. The compact --json has no spaces.

            exit 1
          fi
          echo "ok: embedded semantic search returned a semantic/both match"

        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          path: dist/${{ matrix.asset }}
          if-no-files-found: error

    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          path: dist
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Generate checksums
        run: |
          cd dist
          sha256sum chisme-* > SHA256SUMS
          cat SHA256SUMS

          files: |
            dist/chisme-*

## Linters / formatters: none
No ESLint, Prettier, Biome, oxlint, or `.editorconfig` anywhere. No `lint` or `format` scripts in any `package.json`. The only style enforcement is the writing-style conventions in `CLAUDE.md`, which are unenforced (no tooling backs them).

## Type checking: yes
This is the one static-analysis gate. Every workspace has a `typecheck` script (`tsc --noEmit`), and the root runs them all:
```
bun run --filter '*' typecheck
```
It's a manual command, though, not wired into any hook or CI.

## Test suite: none
No `*.test.ts` / `*.spec.ts` files, no `test`/`tests`/`__tests__` directories, no `test` script, and no test-runner config (no Vitest/Jest, despite Bun having a built-in `bun test`).

The closest thing to a test is in CI: `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs a **smoke test**, but only on `v*` tag pushes (and `workflow_dispatch`), not on regular pushes or PRs. It builds the binary per platform and asserts end-to-end behavior, sync `--limit 5`, then `search ... --json`, and greps for `"matchType":"(both|semantic)"` to catch a broken embedder. There is no CI that runs typecheck, lint, or unit tests on ordinary commits/PRs.

| Linter | None |
| Formatter | None |
| Type checking | `tsc --noEmit` per workspace (manual) |
| Unit/integration tests | None |
| CI on push/PR | None |
| CI on tag | Release build + per-platform smoke test |

content.text:
No, it doesn't. The two workflows are completely decoupled, so a red CI run will **not** stop a release.

Here's why, from the triggers:

- **`ci.yml`** fires on `push` to `main` and on `pull_request`. It never runs on tags.
- **`release.yml`** fires on `push` of a `v*` tag. It has no `needs:` on CI and no awareness of it.

So when you do `git tag v0.2.2 && git push --tags`, the release workflow starts on its own. A failing (or still-running, or never-run) `ci.yml` on `main` has no bearing on it. Branch protection wouldn't help either, tag pushes aren't gated by it.

**What the release *does* gate on** is its own `build` job: it compiles the per-platform binary and runs the smoke test (`sync --limit 5` + `search --json` + grep for a semantic match). The `release` (publish) job has `needs: build`, so if any platform fails to build or the smoke test fails, nothing publishes. But that gate does **not** run typecheck, Biome, or the unit tests. So a type error, lint failure, or broken unit test could still ship as long as the binary compiles and semantic search works end-to-end.

If you want the release blocked when the checks fail, the clean fix is a `check` job at the top of `release.yml` (typecheck + `biome ci` + `bun test`) that `build` then `needs:`. That way a tag push runs the checks first and aborts the whole release if they're red, no duplicated logic, same checks as CI.

Want me to add that gate to `release.yml`? Given a release is coming up, I'd recommend it.

name: release

# Builds and publishes per-platform chisme binaries on a version tag.
#
# We use a per-OS matrix (one native runner per target) rather than cross-compiling
# from a single runner. Reason: the sqlite-vec loadable extension ships as
# per-platform npm packages that only install on a matching host, and build.ts
# embeds that native extension into the binary so semantic search works standalone.
# A single cross-compiling runner would only have its own platform's extension and
# would produce keyword-only binaries for every other target.

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    name: build ${{ matrix.asset }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { runner: ubuntu-latest, asset: chisme-linux-x64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm, asset: chisme-linux-arm64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: macos-15-intel, asset: chisme-darwin-x64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: macos-15, asset: chisme-darwin-arm64, bin: chisme }
          - { runner: windows-latest, asset: chisme-windows-x64.exe, bin: chisme.exe }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.12

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      # Apple's system SQLite (which Bun uses on macOS) is built without loadable
      # extensions, so sqlite-vec can't load and semantic search degrades to
      # keyword-only. Compile a self-contained vanilla SQLite (FTS5 + extension
      # support, depends only on libSystem) for this runner's arch; build.ts embeds
      # it and the binary redirects bun:sqlite to it via Database.setCustomSQLite().
      - name: Build vanilla SQLite for macOS
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ver=3460100
          curl -fsSL "https://www.sqlite.org/2024/sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}.zip" -o sqlite.zip
          unzip -q sqlite.zip
          cc -O2 -dynamiclib \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS3 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS4 \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_RTREE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_COLUMN_METADATA \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_DESERIALIZE \
            -DSQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS \
            -DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 \
            -install_name @rpath/libsqlite3.dylib \
            "sqlite-amalgamation-${ver}/sqlite3.c" \
            -o "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          file "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          otool -L "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib"
          echo "CHISME_MACOS_SQLITE_DYLIB=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/libsqlite3.dylib" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Build native binary
        run: bun run build:cli

      - name: Stage release asset
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          mv "${{ matrix.bin }}" "dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"

      - name: Smoke test (standalone hybrid search end to end)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/dist/${{ matrix.asset }}"
          "$bin" version
          # Index only the newest few checkpoints so the test stays fast as the
          # repo's history grows (chisme sync fetches entire/checkpoints/v1 from
          # origin). Then assert the embedded semantic search actually ran: with a
          # small indexed set, vec KNN returns those checkpoints for any query, so
          # a working embedder yields a "both" or "semantic" match. A broken one
          # yields only "keyword" (or nothing) and fails the build, so a semantic
          # regression cannot ship silently. The compact --json has no spaces.
          "$bin" sync --limit 5
          "$bin" search "semantic search" --json > result.json
          cat result.json
          if ! grep -qE '"matchType":"(both|semantic)"' result.json; then
            echo "::error::smoke test failed for ${{ matrix.asset }}: no semantic match, the embedded embedder may be broken"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "ok: embedded semantic search returned a semantic/both match"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          path: dist/${{ matrix.asset }}
          if-no-files-found: error

  release:
    name: publish release
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          path: dist
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Generate checksums
        run: |
          cd dist
          sha256sum chisme-* > SHA256SUMS
          cat SHA256SUMS

      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          files: |
            dist/chisme-*
            dist/SHA256SUMS
          generate_release_notes: true
